question: Will EU member states approve the screening results for Ukraine's accession clusters 4 and 5 before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: Hungary (Magyar government) has withheld approval of the screening results for clusters 4 and 5 at COELA three times (Oct 20, Oct 27, Nov 10), with no official reason beyond 'needing more time to examine documents'; Moldova is blocked in parallel. Reference class: the Magyar government's 2026 handling of Ukraine's clusters. It held up clusters 2 and 3, then released them within weeks once its stated condition (the education law) was met. Here no condition has been stated, Kyiv says Hungary committed to lifting the veto, and the Irish Presidency is pushing to finish by year-end. Only a Coreper screening approval is needed, not the opening itself, and Coreper meets weekly. Against: three straight refusals, a domestic-politics motive (agriculture cluster), an analyst calling year-end unrealistic, about 7 weeks left, and the risk of slipping to the next presidency. No matching human market found; Polymarket/Manifold contracts on the accession treaty or membership are far-off near-misses and were not used as anchors.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off Coreper approval of the screening results for Ukraine's Cluster 4 (green agenda/connectivity) AND Cluster 5 (resources, agriculture, cohesion), not off the formal opening of the clusters at an IGC. Approval normally passes the COELA working party first, then Coreper.
- Event window: now -> 2027-01-01 per the criteria; as of 2026-11-11, about 7 weeks remain (Coreper meets roughly weekly; the December GAC and European Council fall mid-December; the Irish Presidency ends Dec 31).
- Hungary refused approval at COELA on Oct 20, Oct 27 and Nov 10, 2026 (Kyiv Post; United24; European Pravda, Nov 10: diplomat 'No change'). Moldova's clusters 4/5 screening also not approved.
- Ukraine opened clusters 1 (June 2026), 6 (July 2026), and 2 and 3 (Oct 13, 2026) after amending its education law on Oct 12 to meet a Hungarian minority-language demand (Kyiv Post 87644; European Pravda Oct 12).
- Zelensky and PM Magyar met Oct 16 and agreed to rebuild relations; Hungary blocked clusters 4/5 four days later (Kyiv Post).
- Chentsov (Nov 4): Hungary makes no new minority demands and cites the need to examine chapter documents further. Ukraine's EU envoy (Kachka) says Hungary has no new substantive objections and wants more time; Kyiv says Hungary committed to lifting its veto (Ukrinform/Interfax).
- Diplomat (United24): the Irish Presidency expected no shift on Oct 27 and listed the item mainly to pressure Hungary. The European Council removed firm deadline language.
- Zmina analyst Datsiv (Gwara Media): no official Hungarian explanation; likely domestic political caution; calls opening by year-end 'rather unrealistic' (process takes 3-4 months); Kyiv unclear on what Budapest wants. Magyar: accession is merit-based, not guaranteed.
- Base-rate components: in 2026, Magyar-era holds on clusters 2/3 were released within weeks of Hungary's stated condition being met; for the current hold no condition has been stated. 3 of the last 3 COELA meetings on clusters 4/5 ended in refusal.
- Searched for but not found: a scheduled Coreper date for Ukraine 4/5 screening, Hungarian government statements on timing, any Dec IGC date, and a human prediction market matching this contract.

The Magyar government's 2026 precedent: holds were released within about a month once a stated condition was met. Kyiv says Hungary committed to lifting the veto, the Irish Presidency wants year-end, and officials expect December. calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on all core facts: three COELA refusals, no stated substantive objection, the Cluster 2/3 precedent (about 1 month from block to release once the condition was met), about 7 weeks left, and the Irish Presidency's year-end goal. The remaining disputes are judgment calls on Hungary's motive and on deadline dynamics. The only factual tension, officials expecting a December opening (Run 3, Kyiv Independent snippet) versus an analyst calling year-end unrealistic (Run 1, Gwara Media), cannot be settled without web access; both are credible and are opinion rather than fact. I weight the officials slightly more on timing but discount for the hold having no stated condition and covering Moldova too (suggesting a substantive policy objection). The net is slightly below even, at 0.43. No market anchors this contract.
